label: Capt. Bradford Runyon
narrative: Bradford Runyon is the counterexample this cluster needs, and the board should use him as one. He was the co-pilot of the B-52H, call sign JAG-31, whose crew was vectored onto a radar target northwest of Minot AFB in the early hours of 24 October 1968, and he is named in the contemporaneous debriefing roster alongside radar navigator Maj. Charles Richey, navigator Capt. Patrick McCaslin, electronic warfare officer Capt. Thomas Goduto and gunner TSgt Arlie Judd. What separates him from almost every other witness in this cluster is the direction of contact: the modern investigation of the Minot case exists because Runyon approached the Center for UFO Studies in 2000 of his own initiative and completed a CUFOS questionnaire. Nobody recruited him. That is the opposite of the pattern that dominates the Malmstrom material, and it is why the Minot 1968 case carries the weight it does on this board.
